_note: max_duration_ms updated 2026-08-19 after fixing the OCR crash (scripts/crawler.py's extract_pdf_sync now passes ocr_function=pymupdf4llm.ocr.tesseract_api.exec_ocr instead of letting PyMuPDF4LLM auto-select a RapidOCR backend incompatible with the installed rapidocr_onnxruntime - see requirements.txt). Before the fix this fixture crashed near-instantly (0 words), so the old 300000ms budget was measured against a native-text-only assumption that never actually exercised real OCR. Measured single-pass extraction with real Tesseract OCR on 64 of this document's 166 pages: 1880.8s (~31.3 min) via `python3 -c "...pymupdf4llm.to_markdown(doc, ocr_function=tesseract_api.exec_ocr, ...)"` on the cached body.bin, pymupdf==1.28.2 pymupdf4llm==1.28.2 tesseract 4.1.1. Two-pass determinism checking would take roughly double that plus spawn overhead. Set with wide margin for slower machines; if CI cannot absorb a ~90min-budget PDF fixture, consider excluding this one from default determinism checking rather than lowering the budget below real measured cost.
